subject: ECON
course_description: Applies economic analysis and methods to business problems, using elementary level linear programming, input/output analysis, and game theory. Traditional topics in managerial economics, such as cost and demand analysis, capital budgeting, and cost-benefit analysis.
course_notes: Managerial Economics applies microeconomic theory and quantitative tools to strategic business decisions. Using calculus and Excel analysis, we study net present analysis; demand and cost estimation; pricing strategies including price discrimination, bundling, and tying; entry deterrence, advertising, and other strategic behavior; game-theoretic models of oligopoly; and auction design and bidding. Throughout, we examine how market structure affects managerial choices and how antitrust law constrains them. The course is especially useful for students interested in economic consulting, antitrust and regulatory work, or strategy roles in industry.
